author: Sample commentary (synthetic data)
headline: Spending per resident rose in real terms in almost every department; the largest increases were in homelessness and health.
paragraphs: The lines show real and nominal dollars for the selected departments; the difference between them is inflation. Per-resident spending divides by the January population estimate of each fiscal year, so the 2020–22 population drop pushes it up.

The category breakdown separates salaries, benefits, overtime, non-personnel, aid and capital. Human-welfare departments are mostly 'aid and grants', which is the money that flows to the nonprofits in the first dashboard.

templates.fallback: Too few records match to summarize; widen the years or clear a filter.

caveats.text: Department reorganizations (HSH created FY2017 from DPH and HSA programs) create artificial jumps; the pipeline restates prior years where it can.
